newsitem.title: USA: CBOE elects two new board members, re-elects three.
newsitem.headline: CBOE elects two new board members, re-elects three.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) said Thursday its membership elected two new directors and re-elected three in elections held Wednesday.
The exchange said Thomas Bond, an independent market maker, and David Johnson, a principal at Morgan Stanley & Co, were elected to three-year terms.

Thomas Ascher, an independent market maker; Sherif Nada, president of Fidelity Brokerage Group; and Jack Wing, chairman and chief executive officer of The Chicago Corp, were re-elected to three-year terms.
Two members were also elected to its nominating committee.
The CBOE said independent market makers Merrill Ferguson and David Snyder were elected to the nominating committee, which is made up of six members and a chairman.
On the 21-member board of directors, Bond and Ascher were elected as on-floor directors, Johnson as an at-large director and Nada and Wing as off-floor directors, the CBOE said.
The new board will be effective from the first meeting in 1997, scheduled for January, it said.
